name: Snare
description: a loop of vine on a bent stick. catches small game.

knowledgeLevels.1: You have seen a snare. A loop, a stick, an animal.
knowledgeLevels.2: Materials: vine (muscadine or bush) + stick (tree branch). The loop goes on a game trail.
knowledgeLevels.3: You can make one. Bend the stick, tie the vine, set the loop where they run. Opossums wander into them after dark — the easiest meat you'll ever trap.

name: Deadfall Trap
description: a heavy stone propped on sticks. crushes whatever trips it — set big on a deer trail and it can take a deer.

knowledgeLevels.1: A deadfall. Stone, sticks, bait. Simple and brutal.
knowledgeLevels.2: Materials: 2 sticks + 1 heavy stone + bait (berries or nuts). The trigger is the trick.
knowledgeLevels.3: You can build one. Balance the stone, set the trigger, bait it. Check daily. Set it big on a deer trail and once in a long while it takes a deer — mostly you'll dress rabbit.

name: Box Trap
description: a woven sapling cage with a drop door. for medium game — raccoon, opossum, muskrat, the occasional fox... and sometimes a skunk, which you will regret.

knowledgeLevels.1: A box trap. Woven saplings, a drop door, bait inside. For clever medium game.
knowledgeLevels.2: Materials: 4 sticks + 2 vine + bait (meat scraps work best). The door counterweights shut behind them.
knowledgeLevels.3: You can build one. Set it by dens and water for raccoon and muskrat, on night trails for opossum. Foxes are shy of traps — bait it well, leave it alone, check at dawn. Skunks wander in too: open it from upwind, with a long stick, and have a change of clothes. A rattlesnake in the box means the weave held and your luck did too — pin it before you reach in.

name: Fish Weir
description: stakes and vine woven across shallow water. crayfish funnel in; turtles too.

knowledgeLevels.1: A fish weir. Stakes and vine in the shallows — funnels them in, keeps them in.
knowledgeLevels.2: Materials: 3 sticks + 2 vine. Drive the stakes in a V, leave a gap with the basket at the throat.
knowledgeLevels.3: You can weave one. Set it in creek or wetland shallows. Crayfish pile in; a turtle is a bonus — mind your fingers, they bite.

name: Water Filter
description: cloth and charcoal in a container. makes murky water safe.

knowledgeLevels.1: A filter. Dirty water in, clean out.
knowledgeLevels.2: Materials: cloth + charcoal (from fire) + container. Layer them.
knowledgeLevels.3: You can make one. Cloth on bottom, charcoal, pour through.

name: Cooking Spit
description: a stick over fire. cooks meat evenly.

knowledgeLevels.1: Meat on a stick over fire. Better than raw.
knowledgeLevels.2: Materials: 1 sturdy stick. Green wood (will not burn).
knowledgeLevels.3: You can make one. Cook meat = +50% calories, safe to eat.

name: Stone knife
description: flint knapped to an edge, bound with vine. cuts meat, wood, cord.

knowledgeLevels.1: You have seen a sharp edge. Stone breaks sharp.
knowledgeLevels.2: Materials: stone + vine. Strike the stone to knap an edge, bind it with vine.
knowledgeLevels.3: You can knap one. A few good strikes, a working edge. The oldest tool there is.
